subject: general
question: Which of the following is a term used for species that are not natural residents of the local habitat, but are included in this system?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Exotic.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exotic Species **introduced to new environments often reset the ecological condition in that new habitat.
 
• It threatens the species that exist there.
 
• Hence they are often termed invasive species.
 
• These species compete with local native species for food and cause disease in them.
 
• Lakes and islands are vulnerable to extinction threats from introduced species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abiotic** are those components of the environment that are non-living and affects living organism and the functioning of the ecosystem.
 
• A **biome** is a distinct biogeographical unit consisting of a biological community that has formed in response to a shared regional climate. Biomes may span more than one continent.
 
• **Endemic** is a disease that is regularly found in a particular area or community and is difficult to get rid of. e.g. Chicken pox in UK
